security_audit.summary: I found no evidence of malicious behavior, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or automatic command execution. The static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, public documentation links, placeholder database configuration, and read-only grep suggestions.

static_findings.snippet: **Problem:** Understanding `expire_on_commit` and when objects become stale.
| "greenlet_spawn has not been called" | Lazy loading in async | Use `selectinload`/`joinedload` |
| Stale data | Missing `refresh()` | Call `refresh()` after commit |
| "None is not valid" for UUID | Missing `default_factory` | Add `Field(default_factory=uuid4)` |
expire_on_commit=False,  # Objects stay valid after commit

content.value_statement: SQLModel async projects often fail from lazy loading, schema drift, and session mistakes. This skill gives focused patterns for models, queries, relationships, and ORM debugging.
actual_capabilities: Explains eager loading choices for async SQLAlchemy relationships.
Shows how to separate database models from API schemas.
Documents session state behavior around commit and refresh.
Covers UUID, nullable field, relationship, query, and upsert patterns.
Lists common ORM errors with likely causes and fixes.
Provides grep-based checks for lazy loading and missing query options.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not inspect a repository by itself.
Examples focus on SQLModel with async SQLAlchemy and PostgreSQL patterns.
It does not replace database migration review or production performance testing.
Detection commands are simple text searches and may miss complex query flows.

use_cases.title: Review Async ORM Models
use_cases.description: Check whether models, relationships, schemas, and nullable fields follow practical SQLModel patterns.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Query Performance
use_cases.description: Identify likely N+1 query risks and choose eager loading strategies for collections and single relationships.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Data Shapes
use_cases.description: Create clear create, read, and update schema boundaries that avoid leaking database-only fields.

prompt_templates.title: Review Model Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a new SQLModel design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my SQLModel model design for async usage. Focus on relationships, schemas, nullable fields, and session behavior. Explain the first changes to make.

prompt_templates.title: Find N+1 Risks
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of query performance problems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find likely N+1 query risks in this repository section. Recommend eager loading choices and explain why each choice fits.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Data Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design for a feature with persistence rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SQLModel data access pattern for this feature. Include session boundaries, pagination behavior, UUID handling, and update semantics.

prompt_templates.title: Debug ORM Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation of async SQLAlchemy errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug this async SQLAlchemy failure. Map the error to likely model, relationship, query, or session causes, then propose focused fixes.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why relationship access fails after loading a user.
output: Explain that lazy loading is unsafe in async sessions.
Recommend select-in loading for collections and joined loading for single relationships.
Name the greenlet error as the likely symptom.

output_examples.input: A team wants safer SQLModel schemas for API responses.
output: Separate table models from create, read, and update schemas.
Keep hashed passwords and internal fields out of response schemas.
Use clear naming so request and response shapes are easy to audit.

output_examples.input: An API endpoint returns slow assessment lists for each user.
output: Point to missing eager loading as the first performance suspect.
Recommend checking repeated similar SQL statements in development logs.
Suggest pagination and count patterns for list endpoints.

best_practices: Use eager loading whenever async code needs relationship data after a query.
Keep database table models separate from public API schemas.
Refresh objects after commit when database-generated values are needed.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on lazy relationship access in async SQLAlchemy sessions.
Do not expose password or internal database fields through read schemas.
Do not compare UUID columns to raw strings in query filters.

faq.question: Does this skill run database commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides SQLModel and SQLAlchemy guidance, examples, and simple search suggestions.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits Python projects that use SQLModel, async SQLAlchemy, FastAPI, and PostgreSQL-style models.

faq.question: Can it fix N+1 query issues?
faq.answer: It can recommend eager loading patterns and detection steps. You still need to test the actual query behavior.

faq.question: Does it cover database migrations?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on model, schema, query, relationship, and session patterns.

faq.question: Is it useful with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-neutral and works as context for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it review production security?
faq.answer: Only partly. It helps avoid schema leaks and ORM mistakes, but it is not a full security review.
